data.reasoning: The disagreement was caused by a transient API error in the first model when attempting to audit .nvchecker.toml, leading to an inconclusive result. The second model successfully audited all files, including .nvchecker.toml, and correctly identified them as standard, safe packaging metadata and build scripts with no malicious injections. The PKGBUILD uses standard practices with pinned checksums.
data.disagreement_analysis: The first model (qwen) encountered an HTTP 400 error when auditing .nvchecker.toml and aborted the package verdict as inconclusive. The second model (deepseek) successfully audited the same file and found it to be a benign nvchecker configuration. There is no actual security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .nvchecker.toml due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: The audit orchestrator should implement retries for transient LLM API errors on individual files before marking the entire package audit as inconclusive.
Non-executable configuration files like .nvchecker.toml could be handled with simpler heuristics or regex checks to avoid wasting LLM context and risking API failures.
